chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The child survives for six months, and for seven or nine months, but does not survive for eight months.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the survival of a fetus born after eight months of pregnancy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a specific legal criterion for fetal viability, distinguishing the eight-month pregnancy as an exception where the child is not considered fully viable compared to the six, seven, or nine-month durations. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is foundational for determining inheritance rights and the status of children born to divorced women, reflecting the practical application of prophetic tradition in family law. The distinction highlights the scholarly emphasis on precise temporal markers in defining legal personhood and biological survival.
